technical.lead: Micron quadruples revenue to $41.5B and sells out all 2026 HBM
technical.body: Micron's fiscal-Q3-2026 results, reported June 25, turn the AI buildout into a memory-supply story: revenue of $41.46 billion, up roughly 346% from $9.30 billion a year earlier and well ahead of the ~$35.25 billion consensus, with Q4 guided to about $50 billion. The structural signal is on the high-bandwidth-memory side that feeds Nvidia and AMD accelerators: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said Micron can fill only half to two-thirds of HBM demand and that all of 2026's supply is sold out under multi-year contracts, HBM4 revenue has crossed $1 billion and is ramping about twice as fast as HBM3E, and the quarter included 16 take-or-pay Strategic Customer Agreements locking in roughly $100 billion of minimum contracted revenue plus $22 billion of upfront customer cash. The read-through is that AI compute is now memory-gated, not just GPU-gated.

technical.lead: Qualcomm names Meta as first Dragonfly CPU customer for 2028
technical.body: On June 24 Qualcomm unveiled a full data-center roadmap that for the first time attaches a named hyperscaler to its server-silicon push: a strategic, multi-generation agreement under which Meta plans to use the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000 CPU to power its next-generation server fleet when the part reaches commercial availability in 2028. The roadmap spans the Dragonfly C1000 CPU (claimed >2x better performance-per-watt than existing server CPUs), the Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator (claimed 4x-8x better performance-per-watt than current GPU architectures, sampling 2028), and a new High Bandwidth Compute memory tier Qualcomm says delivers up to a 54x bandwidth jump over its AI200, with 35+ ecosystem partners including Lenovo, Supermicro, Micron, SK hynix and Samsung. The positioning is explicitly an inference-economics attack on Nvidia rather than a training play; the gap is timeline, with first commercial sampling still two years out.

citations.label: Qualcomm - Qualcomm Unveils Comprehensive Data Center Roadmap for the Agentic AI Era with New Dragonfly Portfolio (June 24 2026)

technical.lead: Gartner pegs AI-agent software at $206.5B for 2026, up 139%
technical.body: Gartner's latest forecast pegs AI-agent software spending at about $206.5 billion in 2026 — up roughly 139% from $86.4 billion in 2025 and on track for $376.3 billion in 2027 — a growth rate nearly triple the 47% expansion of overall AI spend, making purpose-built agent software the fastest-growing slice of enterprise software even inside an already-booming market. Gartner pairs the optimism with a standing caution that it expects over 40% of agentic-AI projects to be cancelled by end-2027, so the spend curve and the cancellation risk are rising together. The signal is that agentic software has decoupled from general AI spend as its own line item, concentrating budget and scrutiny on a narrow class of purpose-built tooling.

citations.label: Gartner - Gartner Forecasts Worldwide AI Spending to Grow 47% in 2026

technical.lead: HCLTech leads $234M close, minting $1.5B sovereign-AI unicorn Sarvam
technical.body: The sovereign-AI thesis got a concrete data point this week: HCLTech confirmed it led a $234 million first close of Sarvam's $300 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation — HCLTech's own $150 million check taking a roughly 10.5% stake — minting India's newest AI unicorn. The round funds compute and training for a frontier model targeting coding, agentic and cybersecurity workloads built, hosted and governed inside the country. Set against Gartner's $206.5 billion agent-spend forecast, the deal shows the agent-spend wave is now pulling national-champion model builders, not just US frontier labs, into the capital flow, with a corporate IT-services giant rather than a pure-play VC anchoring the check.

citations.label: HCLTech - Sarvam raises $234 million in first close of $300 million Series B at $1.5 billion valuation

technical.lead: AI World's Fair opens today as summer chip and security dates lock in
technical.body: The forward calendar spans three sub-tracks. Mainstream dev/data: the AI Engineer World's Fair main program runs June 29 through July 2 at Moscone West in San Francisco (~29 tracks, ~300 speakers, 6,000+ attendees), opening today with the Coding Agents keynote and expo, then Autoresearch (July 1) and Harness Engineering (July 2) keynotes; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4. AI-security: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA 2026 and DEF CON 34 with its AI Village run in early August in Las Vegas; OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series stays on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 22-23 at Moscone, Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 in Santa Clara.
